packs.title: Afterlife
packs.subtitle: Sixteen required traditions and corpora, with funerary, scriptural, literary, source-language, metadata, and community-protocol layers kept separate.

slots.label: Pyramid Texts
slots.evidenceNote: Atlas has reviewed academic metadata, but no bounded edition passage for comparison.
slots.gap: A source/edition/witness-linked passage selection is still required.

slots.label: Coffin Texts
slots.evidenceNote: Atlas has reviewed academic metadata, but no bounded edition passage for comparison.
slots.gap: A source/edition/witness-linked passage selection is still required.

slots.label: Book of the Dead
slots.evidenceNote: The cited historical edition segment contains translated declaration material inside Budge's commentary; it is not labeled as a modern critical translation.
slots.gap: The current passage classification is mixed commentary/translation and should not be presented as a witness-level diplomatic text.

slots.label: Amduat
slots.evidenceNote: Museum and academic records identify the work, but Atlas has no bounded translation passage.
slots.gap: Add a rights-reviewed edition and passage-level source chain.

slots.label: Book of Gates
slots.evidenceNote: Institutional metadata identifies the composition; no passage is bundled.
slots.gap: Add a rights-reviewed edition and passage-level source chain.

slots.label: Mesopotamian underworld
slots.evidenceNote: The cited ORACC composite is source-language transliteration, not an Atlas-generated English translation and not one physical tablet.
slots.gap: A reviewed English translation is not bundled.

slots.label: Zoroastrian afterlife
slots.evidenceNote: The Avesta record is linked to Encyclopaedia Iranica, but no edition passage is bundled.
slots.gap: Add source-bounded Avestan and translated passages relevant to judgment and postmortem fate.

slots.label: Greek underworld
slots.evidenceNote: The Odyssey citation is a public-domain historical translation and literary evidence, not a map of one universal Greek afterlife belief.
slots.gap: The segment's content classification remains Unknown and needs editorial review.

slots.label: Jewish traditions
slots.evidenceNote: Daniel 12:2 is one textual position; it does not stand for every Jewish period or community.

slots.label: Christianity
slots.evidenceNote: Revelation 20:5 is one Christian apocalyptic passage and is kept distinct from later systematic teaching.

slots.label: Islam
slots.evidenceNote: The cited historical English translation is evidence for the edition's wording and requires translator-context caution.
slots.gap: The passage needs sura/verse normalization and content-type review.

slots.label: Hindu traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The Katha Upanishad selection engages Yama and death; it is not a summary of all Hindu traditions.
slots.gap: The segment includes editorial framing and still needs content-type review.

slots.label: Buddhist traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The Dhammapada passage is a historical translation and one Buddhist textual voice, not a pan-Buddhist doctrine statement.
slots.gap: Verse boundaries and content type remain to be normalized.

slots.label: Tibetan Bardo
slots.evidenceNote: Atlas retains the Bardo Thodol title as discovery metadata only.
slots.gap: No licensed or public-domain edition passage has been reviewed and bundled.

slots.label: Chinese traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The Infinite Life Sutra selection is a Chinese source-language text. Atlas does not silently present it as an English translation.
slots.gap: A reviewed translation and school-specific interpretive context are not bundled.

slots.label: Lakota sacred narratives
slots.evidenceNote: This community-specific record is represented by public metadata only. It is not a proxy for all Indigenous traditions.
slots.gap: Narrative content and afterlife interpretation are excluded pending community-specific authority and review.

comparisons.title: Postmortem destinations and judgment appear in several bounded sources
comparisons.summary: The cited Egyptian-edition material, Daniel, and Revelation each contain bounded postmortem language. This is a limited thematic comparison, not an equivalence of destinations, persons, or judgments.
comparisons.caution: Shared themes do not prove contact, descent, or borrowing.

comparisons.title: Ritual, resurrection, philosophical, and source-language records answer different questions
comparisons.summary: The Egyptian funerary edition, Christian apocalyptic resurrection passage, and Chinese Buddhist source-language text differ in genre, textual function, and evidence layer.
comparisons.caution: Do not collapse ritual provision, resurrection, literary katabasis, and Pure Land language into one afterlife model.

comparisons.title: Egyptian funerary stages are visible even where texts remain metadata-only
comparisons.summary: Pyramid Texts, Coffin Texts, Book of the Dead, Amduat, and Book of Gates remain distinct stages in Atlas. Only the Book of the Dead currently has a bounded edition citation in this pack.
comparisons.caution: Metadata chronology must not be presented as if all five corpora had equivalent passage coverage.

packs.completionNote: Incomplete: Egyptian, Zoroastrian, Tibetan, and community-specific Indigenous source depth remains visible as metadata or protocol-limited gaps.

packs.title: Creation
packs.subtitle: Requested creation sources remain distinct by genre, language, community, and evidence depth.

slots.label: Egyptian creation traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The selected passage is one Egyptian cosmogonic source in a historical edition, not a universal Egyptian creation account.

slots.label: Enuma Elish
slots.evidenceNote: The ORACC catalogue establishes the work record, but no selected source passage is bundled.
slots.gap: Add a source/edition-bounded passage before using Enuma Elish as comparative textual evidence.

slots.label: Genesis
slots.evidenceNote: Genesis 1:1 is cited from the bundled public-domain edition.

slots.label: Rig Veda
slots.evidenceNote: Atlas links institutional discovery metadata, but no reviewed edition passage.
slots.gap: Add a hymn-specific edition and passage rather than treating the whole Veda as one creation account.

slots.label: Popol Vuh
slots.evidenceNote: The K’iche’ Maya record remains metadata-only under a community-review protocol.
slots.gap: No narrative content may be exported or synthesized without community and edition review.

slots.label: Greek Theogony
slots.evidenceNote: The Perseus-linked work record is present, but no Atlas passage is bundled.
slots.gap: Add a passage-level edition record and translation responsibility.

slots.label: Norse creation
slots.evidenceNote: The Völuspá segment in this historical edition names Ymir and a pre-cosmic gap; it is literary evidence, not proof of a single historic Norse creed.
slots.gap: The segment needs poem/stanza and content-type normalization.

slots.label: Chinese traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The Tao Te Ching selection concerns generative language in one historical translation; it should not be relabeled as a single Chinese creation myth.
slots.gap: Chapter boundaries and content type require review.

slots.label: Kumulipo
slots.evidenceNote: Kumulipo is represented as a Kānaka Maoli genealogy tradition, not generic Polynesian scripture.
slots.gap: Content comparison is blocked pending community-specific authority, version, recorder, and permission review.
slots.community: Kānaka Maoli / Native Hawaiian genealogy tradition

slots.label: Diné creation narratives
slots.evidenceNote: The Diné record is community-specific and metadata-only.
slots.gap: No narrative content is exposed or treated as one fixed scripture.

slots.label: Hopi emergence narratives
slots.evidenceNote: The Hopi record is community-specific and metadata-only.
slots.gap: No narrative content is exposed or universalized.

slots.label: Dinka creation traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The Dinka record requires local community attribution rather than a generic African or Indigenous label.
slots.gap: Content is excluded pending community, version, recorder, and permission review.

comparisons.title: Several available sources describe emergence or ordering
comparisons.summary: The bounded Egyptian and Genesis passages each use generative language, but their agents, genres, and concepts differ.
comparisons.caution: Thematic resemblance alone supplies no evidence of borrowing.

comparisons.title: Cosmogony, scripture, poetry, and philosophical generation are not interchangeable
comparisons.summary: The Egyptian historical-edition translation and the Genesis scriptural translation differ in form and textual function; neither stands for every creation tradition in its wider setting.
comparisons.caution: Comparison preserves genre and translation limits.

comparisons.title: Unavailable and culturally governed sources constrain the preset
comparisons.summary: Enuma Elish, Rig Veda, Theogony, Popol Vuh, Kumulipo, Diné, Hopi, and Dinka records cannot yet support equal passage-level comparison in Atlas.
comparisons.caution: Absence of bundled content is a data limitation, not evidence that a tradition lacks creation knowledge.

packs.completionNote: Incomplete: several required sources are metadata-only, and community-governed narratives remain unavailable for content comparison.

packs.title: Wisdom
packs.subtitle: Practical instruction, scriptural wisdom, philosophical counsel, and community-governed knowledge are compared without treating 'wisdom' as one universal genre.

slots.label: Instruction of Ptahhotep
slots.evidenceNote: A bounded passage from the historical English edition is available.

slots.label: Instruction of Amenemope
slots.evidenceNote: Academic metadata is present without an Atlas edition passage.
slots.gap: Add a rights-reviewed edition and passage selections.

slots.label: Proverbs
slots.evidenceNote: Proverbs 1:1–4 is preserved as a bounded passage in the bundled edition.

slots.label: Ecclesiastes
slots.evidenceNote: The cited passage represents one bounded textual voice on seeking wisdom.

slots.label: Analects
slots.evidenceNote: The cited historical English translation discusses virtue; it is not a stand-in for all Ru/Confucian traditions.
slots.gap: Chapter/section and content-type normalization remain incomplete.

slots.label: Tao Te Ching
slots.evidenceNote: The selected historical translation presents one formulation of sage practice.
slots.gap: Chapter and content-type normalization remain incomplete.

slots.label: Dhammapada
slots.evidenceNote: A bounded passage on hatred and its cessation is available in a historical translation.
slots.gap: Verse boundaries and content type remain to be normalized.

slots.label: Epictetus — Enchiridion
slots.evidenceNote: The selected edition segment distinguishes what is and is not in human power; editorial framing is retained.
slots.gap: The segment mixes introduction and discussion and needs content-type review.

slots.label: Yorùbá Ifá Odu traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The requested broad category is represented by one named community-specific example, not by a universal Indigenous wisdom corpus.
slots.gap: No Odu content is compared pending practitioner/community authority and version-level review.
slots.community: Yorùbá Ifá communities and authorized practitioners

slots.label: Haudenosaunee Great Law / narratives
slots.evidenceNote: This is a distinct Haudenosaunee metadata record and is not conflated with the Ifá example.
slots.gap: Content comparison is blocked pending nation-specific authority and source context.

comparisons.title: Instruction and self-cultivation recur across several available editions
comparisons.summary: Ptahhotep and Proverbs each preserve bounded instructional material while retaining different literary and historical settings.
comparisons.caution: Instructional resemblance is not a lineage claim.

comparisons.title: Wisdom's value is framed differently within the bundled biblical corpus
comparisons.summary: Proverbs opens by commending wisdom and instruction, while Ecclesiastes records the burdens of seeking wisdom. The tension is proposition- and passage-specific, not a claim that either whole work has one simple position.
comparisons.caution: A two-passage tension does not exhaust either work's argument.

comparisons.title: Community-governed knowledge is not filled in by analogy
comparisons.summary: The Ifá and Haudenosaunee records remain separate, protocol-governed metadata slots. Atlas does not infer their teachings from Egyptian, biblical, Chinese, Buddhist, or Stoic sources.
comparisons.caution: Unavailable community content remains a visible gap.

packs.completionNote: Incomplete: Amenemope and both community-governed examples lack passage-level evidence in Atlas.

packs.title: Devil / Evil
packs.subtitle: Adversarial figures, apocalyptic texts, literary reception, modern movements, material imagery, and philosophical evil remain separate evidence categories.

slots.label: Job
slots.evidenceNote: Job 1:6 preserves a bounded occurrence of Satan in its narrative context.

slots.label: 1 Enoch
slots.evidenceNote: The cited historical edition segment refers to Satans; this is not automatically the same role as every later devil concept.
slots.gap: Content-type and section normalization remain incomplete.

slots.label: Gospel of Matthew
slots.evidenceNote: Matthew 4:1 supplies one bounded devil occurrence.

slots.label: Quran
slots.evidenceNote: The cited historical translation uses the form Eblis and must remain translation-specific.
slots.gap: Normalize the sura/verse locator and compare additional translations.

slots.label: Avesta
slots.evidenceNote: A source-linked Avesta work record exists without selected passages.
slots.gap: Add source-bounded Avestan and translated passages before comparison.

slots.label: Codex Gigas Devil portrait
slots.evidenceNote: The National Library of Sweden witness record establishes the manuscript and portrait context; no image is bundled as comparative evidence.
slots.gap: Add a rights-reviewed image/artifact record and iconographic scholarship.

slots.label: Historical demonology
slots.evidenceNote: A broad category label is not a source.
slots.gap: Select specific dated demonological works, editions, passages, and scholarship before making a comparative claim.

slots.label: Lesser Key of Solomon
slots.evidenceNote: The work and Sloane MS 3648 are linked as metadata; operational ritual content is not extracted.
slots.gap: No bounded text passage or reviewed demon classification is included.

slots.label: Dante — Divine Comedy
slots.evidenceNote: The citation is literary reception evidence and is explicitly non-scriptural.
slots.gap: The segment is a table-of-contents context and needs canto-level normalization.

slots.label: Goethe — Faust, Part One
slots.evidenceNote: Mephistopheles appears in a literary work; the citation does not establish religious doctrine.
slots.gap: The bounded segment remains classified as Unknown and cannot support a comparative claim until its source role is reviewed.

slots.label: Milton — Paradise Lost
slots.evidenceNote: This is literary reception evidence, explicitly non-scriptural.
slots.gap: The bounded segment remains classified as Unknown and cannot support a comparative claim until its source role is reviewed.

slots.label: Modern Satanist writings
slots.evidenceNote: Modern movement texts remain metadata-only; their copyright and self-description are respected.
slots.gap: No copyrighted text is reproduced; add licensed excerpts or independent scholarship for claim-level analysis.

slots.label: Hume — Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion
slots.evidenceNote: The cited passage treats the problem of evil philosophically rather than as a demonological entity claim.
slots.gap: The bounded segment remains classified as Unknown and cannot support a comparative claim until its source role is reviewed.

comparisons.title: Adversarial language occurs in distinct textual and later literary contexts
comparisons.summary: The bounded Job and Matthew passages belong to different periods and textual settings. Their sequence does not by itself prove a single line of evolution.
comparisons.caution: Chronology is not a transmission graph.

comparisons.title: Scripture, manuscript imagery, grimoires, and literature are different records
comparisons.summary: The Codex Gigas witness, Lesser Key witness, scriptural passages, and literary works cannot be merged into one demonology source category.
comparisons.caution: A manuscript nickname or portrait does not establish supernatural authorship.

comparisons.title: The philosophical problem of evil is not a demon entity claim
comparisons.summary: Hume's dialogue raises a philosophical challenge about evil, while Job and Matthew contain personified adversarial figures in bounded passages.
comparisons.caution: Do not classify skeptical critique as demonology or as a religious confession.

packs.completionNote: Incomplete: Zoroastrian passages, Codex Gigas imagery, a bounded demonology corpus, and Lesser Key passages remain missing or metadata-only.

packs.title: Anunnaki
packs.subtitle: Ancient attestations, mainstream scholarship, contextual alternatives, and modern popular claims are separated by source category.

slots.label: Ancient Anunna occurrences
slots.evidenceNote: Nine exact ORACC composite transliteration attestations are retained without invented English translations.
slots.gap: These are composite transliterations, not a single witness or complete translation.

slots.label: Mesopotamian mythological contexts
slots.evidenceNote: The ancient occurrence set spans multiple compositions and does not imply one fixed roster or role.
slots.gap: Full composition translations and witness-level context remain incomplete.

slots.label: Mainstream academic scholarship
slots.evidenceNote: ORACC's Ancient Mesopotamian Gods and Goddesses project supplies the bounded scholarly overview.

slots.label: Alternative contextual readings
slots.evidenceNote: The alternatives are bounded contextual readings within scholarship, not ancient-astronaut claims mislabeled as scholarship.

slots.label: Sitchin / ancient-astronaut claims
slots.evidenceNote: Publisher pages establish what Sitchin's modern books claim; they are not evidence about ancient Mesopotamia.

comparisons.title: Ancient divine-name attestations do not state modern extraterrestrial claims
comparisons.summary: The exact ORACC transliterations attest the divine-name spelling in ancient compositions. The publisher pages establish that Sitchin later made Nibiru and ancient-astronaut claims; they do not move those claims into the ancient evidence layer.
comparisons.caution: Atlas does not turn absence in a few lines into a universal negative claim about every Mesopotamian text.

comparisons.title: Modern claims are chronologically and evidentially separate
comparisons.summary: The modern publication claims date to the twentieth and twenty-first centuries; the ancient occurrences belong to Sumerian and Akkadian source contexts. This establishes separation, not a claim about motive.
comparisons.caution: Publisher descriptions are primary evidence for modern claims only.

comparisons.title: Scholarly alternatives concern historical scope and role
comparisons.summary: ORACC's overview and the recorded alternative readings concern a variable divine collective, local pantheons, and later underworld emphasis. They are not endorsements of ancient-astronaut claims.
comparisons.caution: Alternative contextual readings within Assyriology must not be relabeled as popular alternative history.

packs.completionNote: Evidence-ready within the bounded dataset, with explicit limits: the nine attestations are not an exhaustive survey or complete translated corpus.

packs.title: Ethiopian Tradition
packs.subtitle: Canon, textual tradition, church-order works, Meqabyan, and Kebra Nagast are kept community-, edition-, work-, and witness-specific.

slots.label: Greek 1–2 Maccabees records
slots.evidenceNote: The Greek Maccabees records are comparison anchors only and are never used as aliases for Ethiopian Meqabyan.
slots.gap: No bundled passage or community/edition-specific Western canon table is attached to these records.

slots.label: Ethiopian Orthodox canon records
slots.evidenceNote: Community-sourced canon memberships exist for Enoch, Jubilees, Sinodos, Didascalia, and Clement. This does not universalize the enumeration to Eritrean or other communities.
slots.gap: Only selected community memberships are currently modeled; edition-specific enumeration remains incomplete.

slots.label: 1 Enoch and Geʽez textual tradition
slots.evidenceNote: The bundled English historical edition is linked separately from the Geʽez textual-tradition record; it is not represented as a diplomatic Geʽez witness.
slots.gap: A Geʽez witness and modern critical translation are not bundled.

slots.label: Jubilees / Kufale
slots.evidenceNote: The community source and Geʽez textual-tradition record are present without a selected passage.
slots.gap: Add witness-, edition-, and passage-level evidence.

slots.label: First–Third Ethiopian Meqabyan
slots.evidenceNote: The three Ethiopian Meqabyan works have distinct IDs and are not Greek 1–3 Maccabees.
slots.gap: No reviewed edition passages are bundled.

slots.label: Ethiopic Sinodos
slots.evidenceNote: Sinodos is retained as its own church-order compilation record.
slots.gap: No edition or passage is bundled.

slots.label: Ethiopic Books of Covenant
slots.evidenceNote: The Books of Covenant remain a distinct record within the church-order range.
slots.gap: No edition or passage is bundled.

slots.label: Ethiopic Clement
slots.evidenceNote: The listed Ethiopic Clement is not silently equated with every work called Clement.
slots.gap: No edition or passage is bundled.

slots.label: Ethiopic Didascalia
slots.evidenceNote: Didascalia is represented through the named community enumeration.
slots.gap: No edition or passage is bundled.

slots.label: Kebra Nagast
slots.evidenceNote: Kebra Nagast is linked to British Library Or 818 as a physical witness record; no passage is inferred from the witness link.
slots.gap: A rights-reviewed edition and passage selection remain missing.

comparisons.title: Ethiopian Meqabyan remains distinct from Greek Maccabees
comparisons.summary: Atlas uses separate work IDs for First–Third Ethiopian Meqabyan and Greek 1–2 Maccabees. Similar English numbering does not create title or content equivalence.
comparisons.caution: No content comparison is claimed while both sides lack bundled passages.

comparisons.title: Geʽez preservation metadata and English editions are separate layers
comparisons.summary: The Enoch pack slot distinguishes a historical English translation from the Geʽez textual-tradition record. Jubilees currently has only community and recension metadata.
comparisons.caution: A textual-tradition record is not a claim that the bundled English edition derives from one identified Geʽez witness.

comparisons.title: Canon, church order, national epic, and witness context remain separate
comparisons.summary: Sinodos, Books of Covenant, Clement, Didascalia, and Kebra Nagast occupy different work and genre contexts. Their presence in one regional pack does not make them one canon tier or one kind of authority.
comparisons.caution: Ethiopian community evidence is not automatically copied to the independent Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

packs.completionNote: Incomplete: only 1 Enoch has a bundled passage; Jubilees, Meqabyan, church-order works, and Kebra Nagast need edition-level evidence.

packs.title: Indigenous Creation
packs.subtitle: A protocol-first comparison of six community-specific records. Atlas does not expose restricted content or manufacture similarities to fill the corpus gap.

slots.label: K’iche’ Maya — Popol Vuh
slots.evidenceNote: The record is public metadata under a K’iche’ Maya community-review protocol.
slots.gap: No narrative content or influence claim is exported.

slots.label: Diné creation narratives
slots.evidenceNote: The record is public metadata under a Diné community-review protocol.
slots.gap: Version, recorder, audience, permission, and content review remain required.

slots.label: Hopi emergence narratives
slots.evidenceNote: The record is public metadata under a Hopi community-review protocol.
slots.gap: Version, recorder, audience, permission, and content review remain required.

slots.label: Dinka creation traditions
slots.evidenceNote: The regional title cannot replace local Dinka community attribution.
slots.gap: No narrative comparison is made without local source and permission context.

slots.label: Kānaka Maoli — Kumulipo
slots.evidenceNote: Kumulipo is retained as a genealogy tradition with a named cultural authority.
slots.gap: No version is presented as a generic Polynesian creation scripture.
slots.community: Kānaka Maoli / Native Hawaiian genealogy tradition

slots.label: Māori creation genealogies
slots.evidenceNote: The record requires iwi- and hapū-specific authority.
slots.gap: No narrative content or pan-Māori version is inferred.
slots.community: Māori iwi and hapū; specific authority required

comparisons.title: Six communities require six authority and context records
comparisons.summary: K’iche’ Maya, Diné, Hopi, Dinka, Kānaka Maoli, and Māori records each retain their own community authority. A shared discovery pack does not create a pan-Indigenous canon or narrative.
comparisons.caution: Only public metadata is compared; narrative content is not exposed.

comparisons.title: Chronology cannot be normalized from the current metadata
comparisons.summary: The current records do not assert comparable composition dates, performance dates, versions, or recorder histories. Atlas therefore leaves chronological comparison unresolved.
comparisons.caution: Unknown dates are not converted into invented timeline positions.

comparisons.title: Contact, influence, and independent development remain unassessed
comparisons.summary: The pack records no source-level contact evidence among these six community-specific traditions. It therefore provides no borrowing, diffusion, or independent-development verdict.
comparisons.caution: Similarity cannot be assessed from metadata titles, and lack of documented contact in this seed is not proof of isolation.

packs.completionNote: Intentionally incomplete: all six records are metadata-only under community-review protocols, so no narrative-content comparison is presented.
